title: 2000 AMC 12 Problem 1
statement: In the year \(2001,\) the United States will host the International Mathematical Olympiad. Let \(I,\) \(M,\) and \(O\) be distinct positive integers such that the product \(I \cdot M \cdot O = 2001.\) What is the largest possible value of the sum \(I + M + O?\)

solutions.text:
Factoring gives \(2001 = 3 \cdot 23 \cdot 29.\)

To maximize the sum of three distinct positive integers with this product, take \(I = 1,\) \(M = 3,\) and \(O = 23 \cdot 29 = 667.\)

The largest sum is \(1 + 3 + 667 = 671.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: To maximize the sum, make one factor as large as possible and the others small
